rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza reads wa-ʿabada with the bāʾ rounded and ṭāghūt genitive; the other readers use bāʾ with fatḥa and ṭāghūt accusative.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة وحده وعبد الطاغوت بضم الباء وجر التاء والباقون وعبد الطاغوت بفتح الباء ونصب التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a noncanonical reading, al-Hasan and Ibn Hurmuz read mathūbah with a still thāʾ and open wāw, also in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وروي في الشواذ قراءة الحسن وابن هرمز مثوبة ساكنة الثاء مفتوحة الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, al-Aʿmash, and Abān read ʿabuda with ʿayn and bāʾ rounded, dāl open, and ṭāghūt genitive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وابن مسعود وإبراهيم النخعي والأعمش وأبان بن تغلب وعبد الطاغوت بضم العين والباء وفتح الدال وخفض الطاغوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb has a plural verbal reading, ʿabadu al-ṭāghūt.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب عبدوا الطاغوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIkrima's transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās doubles the bāʾ in ʿabada al-ṭāghūt.
rows.anchor: ورواية عكرمة عن ابن عباس وعبد الطاغوت بتشديد الباء وفتح الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubayy and Abū Wāqid are reported to read ʿibād al-ṭāghūt.
rows.anchor: وقراءة أبي واقد وعباد الطاغوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Ruʾāsī reads the phrase passively, like ḍuriba Zayd with its agent unexpressed.
rows.anchor: وقراءة أبي جعفر الرؤاسي النحوي وعبد الطاغوت كقولك ضرب زيد لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAwn al-ʿUqaylī and Ibn Burayda read ʿābid al-ṭāghūt.
rows.anchor: وقراءة عون العقيلي وابن بريدة وعابد الطاغوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlqama's transmission from Ibn Masʿūd reads ʿabd al-ṭāghūt on the pattern ṣarad.
rows.anchor: ورواية علقمة عن ابن مسعود وعبد الطاغوت على وزن صرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary counts ten readings in all, two belonging to the seven canonical readings.
rows.anchor: فهذه عشر قراءات اثنتان منها في السبعة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī parses Hamza's reading under jaʿala, as though God made an idol worshiper among them; jaʿala here means created.
rows.anchor: أبو علي حجة حمزة في قراءة وعبد الطاغوت أن يحمله على ما عمل فيه جعل

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Although ʿabd is not a plural pattern, it is singular in form with a collective meaning, like other definite singular nouns.
rows.anchor: ولكنه واحد يراد به الكثرة ألا ترى أن في الأسماء المفردة المضافة إلى المعارف

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The pattern fiʿl can convey intensity and abundance, portraying repeated, all-out service of the idol.
rows.anchor: بناء فعل يراد به المبالغة والكثرة نحو يقظ وندس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, ʿabada coordinates with laʿanahu in the relative clause.
rows.anchor: وأما من فتح فقال وعبد الطاغوت فإنه عطفه على بناء الماضي الذي في الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular agreement follows the grammatical wording of man rather than its collective meaning, though consistent or mixed agreement would also be valid.
rows.anchor: وأفرد الضمير في عبد وإن كان المعني فيه الكثرة لأن الكلام محمول على لفظه دون معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anomalous mathūbah reading departs from the regular morphological form.
rows.anchor: وأما الوجه في مثوبة فإنه قد خرج على الأصل شاذا

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ compares the irregular form with expressions whose regular analogues would be mathābah and maqādah.
rows.anchor: ومثله ما يحكى عنهم الفكاهة مقودة إلى الأذى وقياسهما مثابة ومقادة

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: He explains mathūbah by moving the wāw's vowel to thāʾ, like maʿūnah; another analysis treats it as a passive-pattern verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وأصل مثوبة مثوبة فنقلت الضمة من الواو إلى الثاء ومثلها معونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line supplies an example for the rare form muḍūfah and its verbal-noun sense.
rows.anchor: وكنت إذا جاري دعا لمضوفة أشمر حتى ينصف الساق مئزري

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan says ʿabd is a plural of ʿabd and adduces a verse about servants' descendants.
rows.anchor: هكذا قال أبو الحسن وقال أحمد

rows.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
rows.claim: Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā analyzes ʿabd as a plural of ʿābid, like bāzil/buzul and shārif/shuruf; ʿibād may also be a plural of ʿabd.
rows.anchor: أحمد بن يحيى: عبد جمع عابد كبازل وبزل وشارف وشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings ʿabad al-ṭāghūt and ʿabadu al-ṭāghūt are straightforward plural constructions.
rows.anchor: وأما عبد الطاغوت وعبدوا الطاغوت فظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀbid al-ṭāghūt and wa-ʿabd al-ṭāghūt can each be singular in form while referring to a group, like ḥuṭam and labad.
rows.anchor: وأما عابد الطاغوت فهو واحد في معنى جماعة وكذلك وعبد الطاغوت لأنه كحطم ولبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathūbah is accusative as a specification, as in khayr thawāban.
rows.anchor: مثوبة نصب على التمييز كذلك هو خير ثوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man can be parsed genitively as an appositive, nominatively as the predicate of an omitted subject, or accusatively as an appositive to the prepositional phrase.
rows.anchor: موضع من يحتمل ثلاثة أوجه من الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The main sense is a worse recompense from God than the consequence of the believers' faith that the opponents denounced.
rows.anchor: أي بشر مما نقمتم من إيماننا ثوابا أي جزاء المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the comparison a worse outcome than that of the Muslims whom the opponents reviled.
rows.anchor: معناه هل أخبركم بشر من الذين طعنتم عليهم من المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording mirrors the opponents' accusation for argument's sake without conceding that believers are evil, like 34:24.
rows.anchor: بشر من ذلك وإن لم يكن في المؤمنين شر على الإنصاف في المخاطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's curse means exclusion from divine mercy.
rows.anchor: أي أبعده من رحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrath means punishment and humiliation for wickedness and disbelief.
rows.anchor: بفسقه وكفره وغضبه عليه أراد به العقوبة والاستخفاف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say God's wrath means imposing humiliation, poverty, and the poll tax on them wherever they lived.
rows.anchor: غضبه أن ضرب عليهم الذلة والمسكنة والجزية أينما كانوا من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making them apes and swine means that they were physically transformed into those animals.
rows.anchor: أي مسخهم قردة وخنازير

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The exegetes identify the apes as the Sabbath-breakers and the swine as the deniers of Jesus' table miracle.
rows.anchor: يعني بالقردة أصحاب السبت وبالخنازير كفار مائدة عيسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Wālibī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Sabbath-breakers' young became apes and their elders became swine.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن الممسوخين من أصحاب السبت لأن شبانهم مسخوا قردة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj coordinates ʿabada with laʿanahu and understands the phrase as those who worshiped the idol.
rows.anchor: الزجاج: هو نسق على لعنه الله ومن عبد الطاغوت

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ supplies an omitted relative pronoun, reading the sense as God made apes and idol worshipers among them.
rows.anchor: الفراء: تأويله وجعل منهم القردة ومن عبد الطاغوت فعلى هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers al-Zajjāj's coordination, since Basran grammarians do not allow the omitted relative pronoun required by al-Farrāʾ.
rows.anchor: وذلك لا يجوز عند البصريين فالصحيح الأول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: They identify ṭāghūt as Satan, whom the people obeyed as if he were worshiped.
rows.anchor: الطاغوت هنا الشيطان عن ابن عباس والحسن لأنهم أطاعوه

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says ṭāghūt is the calf worshiped by the Jews, since the passage describes their traits.
rows.anchor: هو العجل الذي عبده اليهود عن الجبائي لأن الكلام كله في صفتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not support compulsion: creating an unbeliever does not entail creating his unbelief, which the author says God does not create.
rows.anchor: ولا شبهة في أنه تعالى خلق الكافر وأنه لا خالق للكافر سواه غير أن ذلك لا يوجب أن يكون خلق كفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy with making apes and swine fails because God alone creates the physical nature of animals, whereas proof excludes His creating unbelief.
rows.anchor: لأن الدليل قد دل على أن ما به يكون القرد قردا والخنزير خنزيرا لا يكون إلا من فعل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those described as cursed, under wrath, and idol worshipers have the worse place because they end in Saqar; believers have no worse place, as 25:24 says.
rows.anchor: شر مكانا لأن مكانهم سقر ولا شر في مكان المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they are worse than the believers in this life through killing, captivity, humiliation, poverty, and jizya, and in the afterlife through endless punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه أنهم شر مكانا في عاجل الدنيا وآجل الآخرة ممن نقمتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are farther from the straight path and from salvation.
rows.anchor: أي أجوز عن الطريق المستقيم وأبعد من النجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the verse was revealed, Muslims taunted the People of the Book as brothers of apes and swine; they lowered their heads in disgrace.
rows.anchor: فلما نزلت هذه الآية عير المسلمون أهل الكتاب وقالوا يا إخوان القردة والخنازير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Kufans and Yaʿqūb read jazāʾun mithlu with both words nominative and jazāʾ tanwīn; the other readers annex jazāʾ to genitive mithl.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة ويعقوب فجزاء منونا مثل بالرفع والباقون فجزاء مثل ما قتل بالإضافة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī reads nominative mithl as an adjective of the owed compensation, meaning livestock compensation comparable to the game killed.
rows.anchor: أبو علي: حجة من رفع المثل أنه صفة الجزاء والمعنى فعليه جزاء من النعم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: On the nominative reading, min al-naʿam modifies jazāʾ and carries its reference back to the killed game; it cannot be attached after jazāʾ has been qualified.
rows.anchor: على هذه القراءة صفة للنكرة التي هي جزاء وفيه ذكر له

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The genitive reading can be understood as compensation for the game itself, with the annexation idiomatically meaning compensation for what was killed.
rows.anchor: وأما من أضاف الجزاء إلى مثل فإنه وإن كان عليه جزاء المقتول لا جزاء مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verbal noun may be annexed to its object, meaning that an equivalent is recompensed, as in the anomalous accusative reading.
rows.anchor: أي يجازى مثل ما قتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān has a noncanonical reading with jazāʾ tanwīn and mithla accusative.
rows.anchor: قراءة أبي عبد الرحمن فجزاء منون مثل منصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medinan readers and Ibn ʿĀmir read kaffāratu ṭaʿāmi by annexation; the others read kaffāratun ṭaʿāmu, with ṭaʿāmu nominative.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وابن عامر أو كفارة بغير تنوين طعام على الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noncanonical reading attributed to Muḥammad al-Bāqir and Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq uses singular dhū ʿadlin instead of the dual.
rows.anchor: قراءة محمد بن علي الباقر ع وجعفر بن محمد الصادق ع يحكم به ذو عدل منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic construction shows the verbal noun acting on its object after tanwīn, supporting the accusative analysis of mithla.
rows.anchor: بضرب بالسيوف رؤوس قوم أزلنا هامهن عن المقيل لما نون المصدر أعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When ṭaʿāmu is nominative, it is explanatory apposition to kaffārah because food is the expiation itself.
rows.anchor: وأما الوجه في قراءة من رفع طعام مساكين أنه جعله عطفا على الكفارة عطف بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive construction is allowed because the offender chooses among sacrifice, food, and fasting: it is expiation by food rather than sacrifice or fasting.
rows.anchor: ومن أضاف الكفارة إلى الطعام فلأنه لما خير المكفر بين ثلاثة أشياء الهدي والطعام والصيام

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح
rows.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ explains singular dhū as sufficient because one just person could suffice, reading man as applicable to one or two.
rows.anchor: أبو الفتح: فيه أنه لم يوحد ذو لأن الواحد يكفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls Abū al-Fatḥ's grammatical explanation far-fetched and unintelligible.
rows.anchor: إن هذا الوجه الذي ذكره ابن جني بعيد غير مفهوم

rows.speaker: أهل البيت
rows.claim: A report from the two Imams says the just arbiters intended are the Prophet and the authorities after him.
rows.anchor: أهل البيت منقولا عن السيدين ع أن المراد بذي العدل رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the reading's authority is sufficient evidence for its meaning.
rows.anchor: وكفى بصاحب القراءة خبرا بمعنى قراءته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-balaʾ is a test that exposes what is hidden; it can also mean blessing because it reveals whether the recipient gives thanks or disbelieves.
rows.anchor: البلاء الاختبار والامتحان وأصله إظهار باطن الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-bilā means worn or old because it shows the passage of time; al-ghayb is what the senses cannot perceive, including speaking ill of someone absent.
rows.anchor: والبلى الخلوقة لظهور تقادم العهد فيه والغيب ما غاب عن الحواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥurum is plural of ḥarām; muḥrim and ḥarām, and muḥill and ḥalāl, are equivalent; aḥrama can mean entering a sacred month or sanctuary.
rows.anchor: وحرم جمع حرام ورجل حرام ومحرم بمعنى وحلال ومحل كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ḥ-r-m conveys prevention; women are called ḥaram because they are protected, and maḥrūm is one deprived of livelihood.
rows.anchor: وأصل الباب المنع وسميت النساء حرما لأنها تمنع والمحروم الممنوع الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mithl/mithil and shibh/shabah are synonyms.
rows.anchor: والمثل والمثل والشبه والشبه واحد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says naʿam includes camels, cattle, and sheep, though camels alone may be called naʿam; cattle or sheep alone are not.
rows.anchor: والنعم في اللغة هي الإبل والبقر والغنم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ distinguishes ʿadl with fatḥa as an equivalent of a different kind from ʿidl with kasra as a like-for-like equivalent.
rows.anchor: الفراء: العدل بفتح العين ما عادل الشيء من غير جنسه

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basran grammarians use both vocalizations of ʿadl for an equivalent, whether of the same kind or a different kind.
rows.anchor: البصريون: العدل والعدل في معنى المثل كان من الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wabal is heaviness in something unpleasant; food or water may be described as heavy, and the word names a thickener's wooden tool.
rows.anchor: والوبال ثقل الشيء في المكروه ومنه قولهم طعام وبيل وماء وبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted line illustrates that al-wabīl conveys heaviness and describes an imposing animal.
rows.anchor: فمرت كهاة ذات خيف جلالة عقيلة شيخ كالوبيل يلندد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in la-yabluwannakum is an oath particle; partitive min can mean some game, specifically land game during consecration.
rows.anchor: هذه اللام لام القسم ومن في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another partitive explanation is that hunting while consecrated counts as only part of all game.
rows.anchor: أن يكون لما عنى الصيد ما داموا في الإحرام كان ذلك بعض الصيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, min explains the genus, as in the command to shun abomination that is idols.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون من لتبيين الجنس كما تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣayd means the hunted animal, not the act of hunting, because hands and spears can reach an object but not an event.
rows.anchor: وأراد بالصيد المصيد بدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bil-ghayb is an adverbial state meaning someone fears God while unseen; the wording is compared with 50:33 and 67:12.
rows.anchor: في محل النصب على الحال والمعنى من يخافه غائبا كما في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-antum ḥurum is an accusative circumstantial phrase describing the consecrated state.
rows.anchor: في موضع النصب على الحال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Hadyan bāligha al-Kaʿbah is a circumstantial phrase, with the sense that the offering is intended to be brought as a sacrifice.
rows.anchor: منصوب على الحال والمعنى مقدرا أن يهدى قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although bāligh al-Kaʿbah looks definite, it means an indefinite participle; the annexation is non-pure, with tanwīn omitted for ease.
rows.anchor: وبالغ الكعبة لفظه لفظ معرفة ومعناه النكرة أي بالغا الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiyāman is accusative as a specification, meaning an equivalent amount of fasting.
rows.anchor: منصوب على التمييز والمعنى ومثل ذلك من الصيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional has an implicit huwa: whoever repeats the offense, God will punish him; the fa construction occupies a jussive position.
rows.anchor: كأنه قال: ومن عاد فهو ينتقم الله منه لأن الفاء لا تدخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage specifies the general prohibition on hunting for a consecrated person already given at the beginning of the sura.
rows.anchor: لما تقدم في أول السورة تحريم الصيد على المحرم مجملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are singled out because they accept the commandments and benefit from them, though disbelievers are also addressed by religious law; another view says they are disregarded.
rows.anchor: خص المؤمنين بالذكر وإن كان الكفار أيضا مخاطبين بالشرائع لأنهم القابلون لذلك المنتفعون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tests obedience and disobedience by commanding and forbidding, thereby manifesting what is known and making recompense just.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الاختبار من الله أن يأمر وينهى ليظهر المعلوم ويصح الجزاء

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī takes the test to be prohibition of some land game; the commentary compares Muḥammad's community's land-game test with Moses' community's sea-game test.
rows.anchor: عن الكلبي وقد ذكرناه قبل مفسرا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: They identify what hands reach as chicks, young wild animals, and eggs, and what spears reach as larger game.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وهو المروي عن أبي عبد الله ع

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the game is that of the sanctuary, where animals grow familiar with people rather than fleeing as they do outside it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي علي الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the test concerns game nearby and game far away.
rows.anchor: أن المراد به ما قرب من الصيد وما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of fa-yaʿlama is that God treats people as one seeking to know their conduct, displaying justice.
rows.anchor: معناه ليعاملكم معاملة من يطلب منكم أن يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes known what He already knew by bringing the fear into existence; divine knowledge itself does not begin anew.
rows.anchor: فالحدوث إنما يدخل على الخوف لا على العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view says fear of God in the unseen keeps a person from hunting in the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: فينتهي عن صيد الحرم طاعة له تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bil-ghayb here means in solitude and isolation.
rows.anchor: معناه في حال الخلوة والتفرد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the unseen means fear of God's punishment when a person is hidden from sensory observation.
rows.anchor: أن يخشى عقابه إذا توارى بحيث لا يقع عليه الحس عن الحسن

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم البلخي
rows.claim: Abū al-Qāsim al-Balkhī argues that although God eternally knows future deeds, reward or punishment is deserved only when the deed occurs under the commanded conditions, so testing is necessary.
rows.anchor: أبو القاسم البلخي: إن الله تعالى وإن كان عالما بما يفعلونه فيما لم يزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever transgresses God's limits by hunting in the sanctuary or while consecrated faces painful punishment.
rows.anchor: أي من تجاوز حد الله وخالف أمره بالصيد في الحرم وفي حال الإحرام

rows.speaker: أهل العراق
rows.claim: The Iraqis define game as every wild animal, edible or not; they support this usage with ʿAlī's verse about royal hunting, and the author's Imami jurists agree.
rows.anchor: كل الوحش أكل أو لم يؤكل وهو قول أهل العراق

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī's verse contrasts game hunted by kings with heroes hunted in battle.
rows.anchor: استدلوا بقول علي ع: صيد الملوك أرانب وثعالب

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī restricts the prohibited game to animals that may be eaten.
rows.anchor: هو كل ما يؤكل لحمه وهو قول الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥurum can mean consecrated for pilgrimage or ʿumra, or being within the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: أي وأنتم محرمون بحج أو عمرة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the verse prohibits killing game in both consecration and the sanctuary, which the author endorses.
rows.anchor: الجبائي: الآية تدل على تحريم قتل الصيد على الوجهين معا وهو الصحيح

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā says the verse applies only to someone consecrated for pilgrimage or ʿumra.
rows.anchor: علي ابن عيسى: تدل على الإحرام بالحج أو العمرة فقط

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وابن زيد وابن جريج وإبراهيم
rows.claim: They define intentional killing as killing deliberately while forgetting consecration; they say one who remembers being consecrated owes no expiation because the offense is too grave.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن ومجاهد وابن زيد وابن جريج وإبراهيم قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that view, a killer who remembers consecration is too culpable for expiation.
rows.anchor: فأما إذا تعمد القتل ذاكرا لإحرامه فلا جزاء فيه لأنه أعظم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء والزهري
rows.claim: They and most jurists define intentional killing as deliberate whether or not the killer remembers consecration.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وعطاء والزهري وهو قول أكثر الفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Accidental or forgetful killing still incurs compensation according to most exegetes and scholars and the Imams.
rows.anchor: فأما إذا قتل الصيد خطأ أو ناسيا فهو كالمتعمد في وجوب الجزاء عليه

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī says the Qurʾān mentions deliberate killing while the Sunna extends the rule to accidental killing.
rows.anchor: الزهري: نزل القرآن بالعمد وجرت السنة في الخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj allows jazāʾ to be a subject and mithl its predicate, meaning compensation for the act equal to the game killed.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج ويجوز أن يكون المعنى فجزاء ذلك الفعل مثل ما قتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars judge likeness by physical form: an ostrich requires a camel, a wild ass and similar game a cow, and gazelle or hare a sheep; this is the Imami report, and the author prefers this view.
rows.anchor: فالذي عليه معظم أهل العلم أن المماثلة معتبرة في الخلقة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī instead values the killed game fairly and buys equivalent livestock with its price; the author rejects this in favor of likeness in form.
rows.anchor: إبراهيم النخعي: يقوم الصيد قيمة عادلة ثم يشتري بثمنه مثله من النعم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says two upright, learned men from the offender's religious community judge the closest livestock equivalent.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: يريد يحكم في الصيد بالجزاء رجلان صالحان منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offering reaches the Kaʿba by being slaughtered there as a sacrifice.
rows.anchor: أي يهديه هديا يبلغ الكعبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that on reaching Mecca the equivalent is slaughtered and given in charity.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: يريد إذا أتى مكة ذبحه وتصدق به

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The Imami jurists require a game killed during ʿumra to be sacrificed in Mecca opposite the Kaʿba, and one killed during ḥajj at Minā.
rows.anchor: أصحابنا: إن كان أصاب الصيد وهو محرم بالعمرة

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: For food expiation, ʿAṭāʾ says to value the equivalent livestock and distribute its price as food; the author calls this correct.
rows.anchor: أن يقوم عدله من النعم ثم يجعل قيمته طعاما ويتصدق به عن عطاء وهو الصحيح

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda instead says to value the killed game while it is still alive and turn that value into food.
rows.anchor: أن يقوم الصيد المقتول حيا ثم يجعل طعاما عن قتادة

rows.speaker: عطاء والشافعي
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and al-Shāfiʿī say to fast one day for every mudd of food value.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء وهو مذهب الشافعي

rows.speaker: أئمتنا وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: The Imams and Abū Ḥanīfa prescribe one day of fasting per two mudd.
rows.anchor: أن يصوم عن كل مدين يوما وهو المروي عن أئمتنا ع وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Shaʿbī, and al-Suddī take the three expiations to be ordered, with or indicating that the offender must fall under one of them.
rows.anchor: إنها مرتبة عن ابن عباس والشعبي والسدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء والحسن وإبراهيم
rows.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās, with ʿAṭāʾ, al-Ḥasan, and Ibrāhīm, treats the expiations as freely chosen alternatives.
rows.anchor: إنها على التخيير عن ابن عباس في رواية أخرى وعطاء والحسن وإبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imami authorities transmit both views about whether the three expiations are ordered or optional.
rows.anchor: وكلا القولين رواه أصحابنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-yadhūqa wabāla amrihi means that the offender tastes punishment in the afterlife if he does not repent; another view takes it as the painful burden of restitution.
rows.anchor: أي عقوبة ما فعله في الآخرة إن لم يتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although expiation is worship and a benefit, God made the duty heavier after disobedience, as He prohibited fat to the Israelites after their Sabbath violation.
rows.anchor: فثقل ذلك عليه كما حرم الشحم على بني إسرائيل لما اعتدوا في السبت

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God forgave what had happened in the pre-Islamic period.
rows.anchor: من أمر الجاهلية عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation limits forgiveness to the first offense in Islam before the prohibition.
rows.anchor: عفا الله عما سلف من الدفعة الأولى في الإسلام أي قبل التحريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever repeats the consecrated hunt will be punished by God, who can overpower anyone and takes vengeance on transgressors.
rows.anchor: أي من عاد إلى قتل الصيد محرما فالله سبحانه يكافيه عقوبة بما صنع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and the apparent Imami reports say a repeat offender owes no new expiation.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس والحسن وهو الظاهر في روايات أصحابنا

rows.speaker: عطاء وسعيد بن جبير وإبراهيم
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, and Ibrāhīm say the repeat offender must pay compensation; some Imami authorities agree.
rows.anchor: إنه يلزمه الجزاء عن عطاء وسعيد بن جبير وإبراهيم

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash parses alladhīna khasirū anfusahum as an appositive to the object pronoun in la-yajmaʿannakum.
rows.anchor: الأخفش الذين خسروا أنفسهم بدل من الكاف والميم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses alladhīna khasirū anfusahum as a new nominative subject whose predicate is fa-hum lā yuʾminūn, because the gathering includes all people.
rows.anchor: الزجاج هو في موضع رفع على الابتداء وخبره فهم لا يؤمنون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The oath lām may begin a new sentence after the statement that God prescribed mercy, or explain that mercy as postponing the gathering to allow repentance.
rows.anchor: واللام في ليجمعنكم لام قسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to travel and look means to observe with the eyes and reflect with the heart on the fate of earlier deniers.
rows.anchor: والنظر طلب الإدراك بالبصر وبالفكر وبالاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruins of past peoples and widely known reports of their destruction remained available; seeing and hearing them should prompt belief and deter unbelief.
rows.anchor: لأن ديار المكذبين من الأمم السالفة كانت باقية وأخبارهم في الخسف والهلاك كانت شائعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether the heavens and earth belong to God who created them or to idols; Muḥammad must answer that they belong to God, who creates, owns, and governs them.
rows.anchor: الله الذي خلقهما أم الأصنام فإن أجابوك فقالوا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains that God prescribed mercy upon Himself as a commitment to beneficence toward creation.
rows.anchor: أي أوجب على نفسه الإنعام على خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says God obligated Himself to reward obedience.
rows.anchor: أوجب على نفسه الثواب لمن أطاعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another says God obligated Himself to show mercy by giving people time to repent.
rows.anchor: أوجب على نفسه الرحمة بأنظاره عباده وإمهاله إياهم ليتداركوا ما فرطوا فيه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says God promised Muḥammad's community that He would delay punishment for disbelief until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: بل يؤخرهم إلى يوم القيامة عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gathering them to the Resurrection may explain mercy as postponement that gives sinners time to repent.
rows.anchor: أي ليؤخرن جمعكم إلى يوم القيامة فيكون تفسيرا للرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the gathering is an argument against those who deny resurrection, joining later generations with earlier ones on the day they reject.
rows.anchor: إن هذا احتجاج على من أنكر البعث والنشور ويقول ليجمعنكم إلى اليوم

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the verse specifically threatens the polytheists who lose themselves by gathering them on the day they deny.
rows.anchor: معناه ليجمعن هؤلاء المشركين الذين خسروا أنفسهم إلى هذا اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning works as an inescapable argument even though disbelievers reject resurrection, and follows the proof already given.
rows.anchor: والجواب أنه جار مجرى الإلزام وأيضا فإنه تعالى إنما ذكر ذلك عقيب الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction in saying the Resurrection has no doubt although a disbeliever doubts it: truth remains true despite a denier's uncertainty.
rows.anchor: والجواب أن الحق حق وإن ارتاب فيه المبطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evidence removes doubt: worldly blessings reach both good and evil, so another realm must distinguish them.
rows.anchor: فإن نعم الدنيا تعم المحسن والمسىء فلا بد من دار يتميز فيه المحسن من المسىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reward must be delivered in an afterlife free of worldly impurities because it cannot be joined to the hardship inherent in religious obligation.
rows.anchor: وإذا لم يمكن إيصال الثواب في الدنيا لأن من شأنه أن يكون صافيا من الشوائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enabling oppression without earthly redress, and causing illness without compensation here, require another realm where compensation is paid and victims receive justice.
rows.anchor: وإنزال الأمراض من غير استحقاق ولا ايفاء عوض في العاجل
